question: Who built an ark before the great flood?
explanation: Noah built the ark as God instructed, bringing his family and the animals to safety.
source: Genesis 6–9

question: At which town was Jesus born?
explanation: Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea during the reign of King Herod.
source: Matthew 2:1

question: Which prophet spent three days and nights inside a great fish?
explanation: Jesus later pointed to Jonah's three days in the fish as a sign of His own three days in the tomb (Matthew 12:40).
source: Jonah 1:17; Matthew 12:40

question: Which young shepherd defeated the giant Goliath?
explanation: David picked five smooth stones from a brook but needed only one, telling Goliath that "the battle is the Lord's" (1 Samuel 17:40, 47).
source: 1 Samuel 17

question: Where did Jesus turn water into wine?
explanation: John calls it the first of Jesus' signs, and it began with His mother telling the servants, "Whatever He says to you, do it" (John 2:5, 11).
source: John 2:1–11

question: How many apostles did Jesus appoint during His ministry?
explanation: Their number echoes the twelve tribes of Israel, and Jesus promised they would one day sit on twelve thrones (Matthew 19:28).
source: Mark 3:13–19; Matthew 19:28

question: Who was thrown into a den of lions for praying to God?
explanation: Daniel kept praying three times a day by his open window, and God sent His angel to shut the lions' mouths (Daniel 6:10, 22).
source: Daniel 6

question: Which disciple denied knowing Jesus three times?
explanation: After the Resurrection, Jesus asked Peter "Do you love Me?" three times, lovingly restoring him (John 21:15–17).

question: In the parable of the Prodigal Son, what job did the son take when his money ran out?
explanation: He was hungry enough to long for the pigs' food, yet when he came home his father ran to embrace him "when he was still a great way off" (Luke 15:16, 20).

question: Which tax collector climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus?
explanation: He was short, so he ran ahead of the crowd; after Jesus came to his house, he promised to repay anyone he had cheated fourfold (Luke 19:3–8).

question: Who was anointed as the first king of Israel?
explanation: The prophet Samuel anointed him, and he came from the tribe of Benjamin, the same tribe as the apostle Paul, who was also named Saul (Philippians 3:5; Acts 13:9).
source: 1 Samuel 9–10

question: What did Jesus multiply to feed the five thousand?
options: Seven loaves and a few fish
Twelve loaves and a jar of oil
explanation: John adds that the barley loaves came from a young boy, and twelve baskets of leftovers were gathered afterward (John 6:9, 13).
source: Matthew 14:13–21; John 6:1–13

question: Which prophet was taken up to heaven in a whirlwind?
explanation: A chariot of fire appeared, and his disciple Elisha, who had asked for a double portion of his spirit, picked up the mantle that fell from him (2 Kings 2:9–13).
source: 2 Kings 2:1–14

question: Who prayed for a child at Shiloh and became the mother of the prophet Samuel?
explanation: Her joyful song of thanksgiving in 1 Samuel 2 has many echoes in Mary's Magnificat (Luke 1:46–55).
source: 1 Samuel 1:1–2:10

question: Saul met the risen Jesus on the road to which city?
explanation: Blinded for three days, he was healed and baptized after a disciple named Ananias laid hands on him (Acts 9:9, 17–18).
source: Acts 9:1–19

question: Which river did Joshua lead Israel across into the Promised Land?
explanation: The waters stopped flowing as soon as the priests carrying the Ark stepped in, and twelve stones were set up as a memorial (Joshua 3:15–16; 4:1–9).
source: Joshua 3–4

question: Which woman sat at Jesus' feet listening while her sister was busy serving?
explanation: When Martha asked for help, Jesus gently told her that Mary had chosen "that good part" (Luke 10:42).

question: Which Roman centurion's household received the Holy Spirit as Peter preached to them?
explanation: Just before, Peter saw a vision of a sheet full of animals, which taught him that "God shows no partiality" (Acts 10:34).
source: Acts 10

question: The Ethiopian official baptized by Philip served under which queen?
explanation: "Candace" (Kandake) was the title of the queens of ancient Kush, and the official was reading Isaiah 53 in his chariot when Philip ran up to him (Acts 8:28–35).

question: What was the name of the servant whose ear Peter cut off in Gethsemane?
explanation: Only John gives his name, while Luke, the physician, records that Jesus touched the ear and healed him (Luke 22:51).

question: Which judge of Israel asked God for a sign using a fleece of wool?
explanation: God later trimmed Gideon's army to just 300 men so Israel would know the victory came from Him (Judges 7:2, 7).

question: Which young man fell from a window during Paul's long sermon and was restored to life?
explanation: He dozed off and fell from the third story; fittingly, his Greek name means "fortunate" (Acts 20:9–12).

question: Which evangelist is traditionally known as the founder of the Church in Alexandria?
explanation: The Coptic Church traces its apostolic foundation in Alexandria to Saint Mark the Evangelist.
source: Coptic Orthodox tradition: Saint Mark, founder of the See of Alexandria

question: In which country did the Coptic Church first take root?
explanation: The Coptic Church has its roots in Egypt, with Alexandria as its historic apostolic see.
source: History of the Coptic Orthodox Church of Alexandria

question: The Coptic Pope's official title names him Pope of which city?
explanation: His full title is Pope of Alexandria and Patriarch of the See of St. Mark, even though the papal residence is now in Cairo.
source: Official title of the Coptic Orthodox Pope: Pope of Alexandria and Patriarch of the See of St. Mark

question: Whose threat led the Holy Family to flee into Egypt?
explanation: Copts treasure this visit: the Feast of the Entry of the Lord into Egypt is kept on 24 Bashans (June 1), and churches stand all along the route tradition says they took.
source: Matthew 2:13–15; Coptic feast of the Entry of the Lord into Egypt (24 Bashans)

question: Which pope led the Coptic Church from 1971 to 2012?
explanation: Both as Bishop of Christian Education and as pope, he was famous for weekly Wednesday meetings where people of all ages brought him their questions.
source: Coptic Orthodox Church: Pope Shenouda III, 117th Pope (enthroned 14 Nov 1971, reposed 17 Mar 2012)

question: Who became Pope of Alexandria in November 2012?
explanation: He was chosen by altar lot: during the Divine Liturgy, a blindfolded child drew his name from among the three final candidates.
source: Coptic Orthodox Church: altar lot of 4 Nov 2012; enthronement of Pope Tawadros II, 18 Nov 2012

question: Wadi el-Natrun in Egypt's Western Desert is famous for what?
explanation: Known to early Christians as Scetis, it still has four active monasteries that have welcomed monks and pilgrims since the 4th century.
source: Coptic monastic history: the monasteries of Wadi el-Natrun (Scetis)

question: What famous statement of faith came from the Council of Nicaea?
explanation: Copts still pray it in the Agpeya, the Book of Hours, beginning with the words "We believe in one God."
source: Council of Nicaea (AD 325); Agpeya (Coptic Book of Hours)

question: In what year did the Council of Nicaea meet?
explanation: It was the first ecumenical council, and Church tradition remembers its bishops as "the 318 Fathers."
source: Council of Nicaea (AD 325); tradition of the 318 Fathers of Nicaea

question: Which young Alexandrian deacon defended Christ's divinity against Arius at Nicaea?
explanation: He went as deacon and secretary to Pope Alexander, and just three years later he became Pope of Alexandria himself.
source: Council of Nicaea (AD 325); Socrates Scholasticus, Church History 1.8 and 1.15

question: Which council, led by St. Cyril in AD 431, affirmed Mary as Theotokos?
explanation: Theotokos means "God-bearer" or Mother of God, a title Copts sing joyfully in the Theotokias of the Midnight Praises.
source: Council of Ephesus (AD 431)

question: The Council of Constantinople (AD 381) expanded the Creed especially about whom?
explanation: It added the words confessing the Holy Spirit as "the Lord, the Giver of Life," worshipped and glorified with the Father and the Son.
source: First Council of Constantinople (AD 381); Niceno-Constantinopolitan Creed

question: The Coptic Church did not accept which council held in AD 451?
explanation: The Coptic Church, with the other Oriental Orthodox churches, did not accept Chalcedon; in recent decades these churches have held warm theological dialogues with churches that did.
source: Council of Chalcedon (AD 451); Oriental Orthodox churches' position on Chalcedon

question: Which famous school in Alexandria was led by teachers like Clement and Origen?
explanation: Coptic tradition traces it back to St. Mark; its first known head was Pantaenus, and Origen took charge of teaching there at just 18.
source: Eusebius, Church History 5.10 and 6.3; St. Jerome, On Illustrious Men 36

question: The Coptic alphabet is mainly based on which alphabet?
explanation: Scribes added a handful of letters from Demotic, the older Egyptian script, for sounds Greek lacked, such as shai for "sh."
source: Coptic alphabet: Greek letters plus Demotic-derived letters

question: The word "Copt" comes from a Greek word meaning what?
explanation: Greek Aigyptios became qibt in Arabic and "Copt" in English, so the Coptic Church is, by name, the Church of the Egyptians.
source: Etymology: Greek Aigyptios → Arabic qibt → Copt

question: The Coptic "Era of the Martyrs" counts years from which emperor's reign?
explanation: Year 1 of the Coptic calendar is AD 284, when Diocletian came to power; his persecution was so fierce that Copts chose to count time by their martyrs.
source: Coptic calendar, Anno Martyrum (counted from AD 284)

question: Pope Tawadros II is which numbered Pope of Alexandria?
explanation: The count runs unbroken from St. Mark, the first, through Pope Kyrillos VI (116th) and Pope Shenouda III (117th).
source: Coptic Orthodox Church, list of the Popes of Alexandria

question: By tradition, which shoemaker was St. Mark's first convert in Alexandria?
explanation: Tradition says Mark healed Anianus's hand after an awl pierced it; Anianus later became the second Pope of Alexandria.
source: Coptic Synaxarium, 20 Hathor (Pope Anianus); Coptic tradition

question: Which Coptic dialect is mainly used in the Church's liturgy today?
explanation: Bohairic comes from the western Nile Delta and has been the Church's main liturgical dialect since about the 11th century, when it replaced Sahidic.
source: History of the Coptic language: Bohairic as liturgical dialect

question: Coptic tradition says the Holy Family's longest stay in Egypt was where?
explanation: Tradition says they lived about six months at the site of today's al-Muharraq Monastery near Assiut, and its ancient church is honored as the house where they stayed.
source: Coptic tradition (Vision of Pope Theophilus); Monastery of the Virgin Mary, al-Muharraq

question: In AD 367, whose Festal Letter listed the 27 New Testament books?
explanation: His 39th Festal Letter, sent to announce the date of Pascha, is the earliest known list matching exactly today's 27 New Testament books.
source: St. Athanasius, 39th Festal Letter (AD 367)

question: Which Egyptian saint is often called the father of monasticism?
explanation: Saint Anthony the Great became a model for Christian monastic life in the Egyptian desert.
source: Saint Athanasius, Life of Anthony

question: Who is known as the first Christian martyr?
explanation: The book of Acts describes Stephen’s witness and martyrdom.
source: Acts 6–7

question: "Mar Girgis" is the Arabic name of which saint?
explanation: Copts call him the Prince of Martyrs, and his icons show him on horseback slaying a dragon, a picture of good triumphing over evil.
source: Coptic Synaxarium, 23 Baramouda (St. George, Prince of Martyrs)

question: Before his conversion, St. Moses the Black was known as what?
explanation: Later, asked to judge a brother, he arrived carrying a leaking jug of water and said, "My sins run out behind me and I do not see them," and the brother was forgiven.
source: Sayings of the Desert Fathers (Alphabetical Collection), Abba Moses

question: St. Stephen was one of seven men chosen to serve as what?
explanation: The Coptic Church honors him as St. Stephen the Archdeacon, and Acts says his face shone "like the face of an angel."

question: According to St. Jerome, what creature brought St. Paul the Hermit bread?
explanation: Jerome writes that the raven brought half a loaf every day for sixty years, and a whole loaf on the day St. Anthony came to visit.
source: St. Jerome, Life of Paul the First Hermit 10

question: After hearing a Gospel reading in church, what did young St. Anthony do?
explanation: He heard Jesus say, "Go, sell what you have and give to the poor," took it to heart, and later withdrew into the desert.
source: St. Athanasius, Life of Anthony 2; Matthew 19:21

question: St. Pachomius is remembered as the founder of which kind of monastic life?
explanation: A former Roman soldier, he gathered monks at Tabennisi in Upper Egypt to pray and work together under a shared rule, a model later followed far beyond Egypt.
source: Bohairic Life of Pachomius; Palladius, Lausiac History 32

question: St. Macarius the Great pioneered monastic life in which desert?
explanation: He settled there around AD 330, and the Monastery of St. Macarius still prays in the same valley today.
source: Palladius, Lausiac History 17; Coptic monastic tradition

question: By Coptic tradition, St. Demiana was martyred together with how many virgins?
explanation: She is honored as a mother of monastic life for Coptic women, and her monastery near Bilqas in the Nile Delta draws many pilgrims.
source: Coptic Synaxarium, 13 Toba (St. Demiana and the forty virgins)

question: What title does the Coptic Church give St. Athanasius?
explanation: He stood so firmly for the faith of Nicaea that a famous saying grew up about him: "Athanasius against the world."
source: Coptic Orthodox tradition (St. Athanasius the Apostolic, 20th Pope of Alexandria)

question: Which Pope of Alexandria is known as the "Pillar of Faith"?
explanation: St. Cyril, nephew of Pope Theophilus, championed the title Theotokos, and his writings about Christ are still treasured today.
source: Coptic Synaxarium entry for St. Cyril I, 24th Pope of Alexandria (copticchurch.net)

question: St. Mary of Egypt turned to God after she could not enter a church in which city?
explanation: An unseen force kept her at the door on the Feast of the Cross; after praying before an icon of the Virgin she entered, then lived about 47 years in the desert beyond the Jordan.
source: St. Sophronius of Jerusalem, Life of St. Mary of Egypt

question: Coptic tradition links St. Simon the Tanner to which miracle?
explanation: Copts still remember it with three extra days added to the Nativity Fast, and a great cave church in the Mokattam hills bears his name.
source: History of the Patriarchs (Pope Abraham ibn Zar'a, 10th century); Coptic tradition

question: Which 20th-century pope, famed for praying the liturgy daily, is honored as a saint?
explanation: He loved St. Mina dearly and founded the Monastery of St. Mina at Mariout in 1959; the Holy Synod recognized him as a saint in 2013.
source: Coptic Holy Synod decision (20 June 2013); Monastery of St. Mina, Mariout (founded 1959)

question: How many martyrs are honored together as the Martyrs of Libya (2015)?
explanation: Pope Tawadros II added them to the Synaxarium within days, and in 2023 Pope Francis added them to the Catholic Roman Martyrology, a rare shared honor.
source: Coptic Synaxarium (commemorated 15 February); Roman Martyrology addition announced 11 May 2023

question: St. Athanasius was sent into exile how many times?
explanation: Four different emperors banished him, yet he used those years well, at one point hiding among the desert monks he loved.
source: Socrates Scholasticus, Church History, Books 1–4; St. Athanasius, Apology for His Flight

question: According to St. Athanasius, about how old was St. Anthony when he died?
explanation: Athanasius adds that even at that age Anthony's eyes were undimmed and he had not lost a single tooth, though they were worn down.
source: St. Athanasius, Life of Anthony 89, 93

question: Which Desert Mother has sayings recorded in the Sayings of the Desert Fathers?
explanation: She taught that "in the beginning there is struggle" for those who draw near to God, "but after that, indescribable joy."
source: Sayings of the Desert Fathers (Alphabetical Collection), Amma Syncletica

question: St. Shenouda the Archimandrite led which great monastery near Sohag?
explanation: His sermons and letters in Sahidic Coptic make him one of the greatest writers in the whole Coptic language.
source: Besa, Life of Shenoute

question: What language, alongside Arabic, is traditionally used in Coptic Orthodox worship?
explanation: Coptic, the latest stage of the ancient Egyptian language, remains a liturgical language of the Church.
source: Coptic Orthodox liturgical tradition

question: What does the word “liturgy” refer to in church life?
options: The public worship of the Church
explanation: Liturgy refers to the Church’s communal worship; the Divine Liturgy centers on the Eucharist.
source: Christian liturgical terminology

question: Which direction do Coptic churches traditionally face for prayer?
explanation: Christ is called the "Sun of Righteousness," and He said His coming will be like lightning from the east, so Copts pray toward the sunrise.
source: Malachi 4:2; Matthew 24:27; Coptic church architecture

question: Most of the Agpeya's prayers come from which book of the Bible?
explanation: Each hour pairs psalms with a Gospel reading, echoing David's words, "Seven times a day I praise You."
source: Agpeya (Coptic Book of Hours); Psalm 119:164

question: What is the sanctuary with the altar called in a Coptic church?
explanation: Haikal means "temple," and larger Coptic churches often have three haikals side by side, each with its own altar.
source: Coptic church architecture

question: How many sacraments (mysteries) does the Coptic Church celebrate?
explanation: They are Baptism, Chrismation, Eucharist, Confession, Unction of the Sick, Matrimony and Priesthood, called "mysteries" because God's grace works in them unseen.
source: Coptic Orthodox teaching on the Seven Holy Mysteries

question: What does "Kyrie eleison" mean?
explanation: Each Agpeya hour prays it 41 times, a number Coptic tradition links to Christ's 39 lashes, the crown of thorns and the spear.
source: Agpeya (Coptic Book of Hours)

question: What is the Tasbeha?
explanation: Tasbeha is Arabic for "praise"; it weaves biblical canticles with hymns to St. Mary called Theotokias, and many churches pray it on Saturday nights before the Sunday Liturgy.
source: The Holy Psalmody (Coptic Tasbeha book)

question: Which liturgy is prayed most often in the Coptic Church?
explanation: The Church has three liturgies: St. Basil for most days, St. Gregory especially on major feasts, and the ancient Alexandrian Liturgy of St. Cyril, prayed more rarely.
source: Coptic Euchologion (Kholagi)

question: What is the Eucharistic bread called in the Coptic Church?
explanation: Its stamp shows a large central cross, the Isbodikon, circled by twelve small crosses for the apostles, and the priest chooses the finest loaf as "the Lamb."
source: Coptic Euchologion: Offertory and Selection of the Lamb

question: Which Coptic deacon rank's name means "chanter" or "hymn singer"?
explanation: It is the first rank, often given to children, followed by Anagnostis (reader), subdeacon, deacon and archdeacon.
source: Coptic Orthodox ranks of the deaconate

question: "Metanoia," the word Copts use for a prostration, means what?
explanation: Prostrations are not made on Sundays or during the joyful Fifty Days after the Resurrection, a custom already noted at the Council of Nicaea.
source: Greek metanoia; Council of Nicaea (AD 325), Canon 20

question: Which mystery does a Coptic child receive right after Baptism?
explanation: The priest anoints the newly baptized with the holy Myron oil, sealing them with the gift of the Holy Spirit, and they then receive Holy Communion.
source: Coptic rite of Baptism and Chrismation (Holy Myron)

question: During most Coptic fasts, believers abstain from what?
explanation: Fish is allowed in some fasts, like the Nativity and Apostles' Fasts, but not in Great Lent, and fasting also means going without food until a set hour.
source: Coptic Orthodox fasting practice

question: Which two instruments traditionally accompany Coptic hymns?
explanation: Deacons keep the rhythm with them, and many Coptic hymns have been handed down by ear for centuries.
source: Coptic hymnody tradition

question: The name "Agpeya" comes from a Coptic word meaning what?
explanation: The Agpeya gathers prayers for the hours of the day, from the First Hour at sunrise all the way to the Midnight prayer.
source: Agpeya (Coptic Book of Hours); Coptic agp, "hour"

question: Which Agpeya hour especially remembers the Holy Spirit's descent at Pentecost?
explanation: Acts says the Spirit came at "the third hour of the day," about 9 a.m.; the Sixth Hour remembers the Crucifixion and the Ninth, Christ's death on the Cross.
source: Agpeya, Third Hour (Terce); Acts 2:15

question: How many Hoses (biblical canticles) are in the Midnight Praises?
explanation: They are the Song of Moses at the Red Sea, Psalm 136, the Song of the Three Young Men, and Psalms 148–150.
source: The Holy Psalmody (Tasbeha); Exodus 15; Psalm 136; Daniel 3; Psalms 148–150

question: In the Coptic Liturgy, the reading from the Book of Acts is called what?
explanation: Praxis is Greek for "acts"; it follows the readings from St. Paul's letters (the Pauline) and the general epistles (the Catholicon).
source: Coptic Katameros (lectionary): Liturgy of the Word

question: Which hymn is chanted twelve times in each hour of Holy Week (Pascha)?
explanation: Its words, "Thine is the power and the glory and the blessing and the majesty forever, Amen," echo the praise of heaven in Revelation.
source: Coptic Holy Week (Pascha) rite; Revelation 5:12–13

question: What does the Feast of the Resurrection celebrate?
explanation: The Feast of the Resurrection celebrates Jesus Christ’s victory over death.
source: Matthew 28:1–10

question: The Feast of Theophany commemorates which event?
options: The feeding of the five thousand
explanation: Theophany celebrates Christ’s baptism in the Jordan and the revelation of the Holy Trinity.
source: Matthew 3:13–17; Coptic Orthodox feast calendar

question: On Palm Sunday, Jesus rode into Jerusalem on which animal?
explanation: This fulfilled Zechariah 9:9, and only John's Gospel specifies that the branches the crowd waved were palms (John 12:13).
source: Matthew 21:1–11; John 12:12–15; Zechariah 9:9

question: What does the Feast of Pentecost celebrate?
options: The birth of John the Baptist
explanation: Pentecost means "fiftieth" in Greek: it falls on the fiftieth day counting from the Resurrection, when the Spirit came as tongues of fire (Acts 2:1–4).
source: Acts 2:1–41

question: How many days after the Resurrection did Jesus ascend into heaven?
explanation: Counting Resurrection Sunday as the first day, the Feast of the Ascension always lands on a Thursday.

question: Great Lent's forty days recall Jesus fasting where?
explanation: In the Coptic Church, Great Lent stretches to 55 days: a preparation week, the Holy Forty, and Holy Week.
source: Matthew 4:1–2; Coptic Orthodox fasting tradition (Great Lent, 55 days)

question: What does the Feast of the Annunciation celebrate?
options: The birth of John the Baptist
explanation: Gabriel came "in the sixth month" of Elizabeth's pregnancy, and the Copts keep the feast on 29 Baramhat, about nine months before the Nativity on 29 Kiahk.
source: Luke 1:26–38; Coptic Orthodox calendar: Annunciation on 29 Baramhat (7 April)

question: In the Coptic Orthodox Church, the Nativity is celebrated on which Gregorian date?
explanation: The Copts keep it on 29 Kiahk, which matches 25 December on the older Julian calendar: the same feast, counted on a different calendar.
source: Coptic Orthodox calendar: Nativity on 29 Kiahk (7 January)

question: What is Nayrouz in the Coptic Church?
options: The end of the Apostles' Fast
The start of the month of Kiahk
explanation: It falls on 1 Thout, usually 11 September, and opens a year numbered A.M., Anno Martyrum, the "Year of the Martyrs."
source: Coptic Orthodox calendar: Nayrouz on 1 Thout (11 September; 12 September in the year before a leap year)

question: How many days does the Coptic Fast of Nineveh last?
explanation: It recalls Nineveh repenting at Jonah's preaching, and it ends with the feast of "Jonah's Passover" on the Thursday.
source: Jonah 3:4–10; Coptic Orthodox calendar: Fast of Nineveh (Monday–Wednesday, two weeks before Great Lent)

question: The Apostles' Fast ends on the feast of which two apostles?
explanation: It starts the day after Pentecost and ends on 5 Epep (12 July), so its length shifts each year with the date of the Resurrection.
source: Coptic Orthodox calendar: Feast of the Apostles Peter and Paul, 5 Epep (12 July)

question: The Feast of the Cross recalls the finding of the True Cross by which empress?
explanation: Helena was the mother of Emperor Constantine, and the Coptic Church keeps this feast on 17 Thout, usually 27 September.
source: Coptic Synaxarium, 17 Thout; Coptic Orthodox calendar: Feast of the Cross (27 September)

question: In the Coptic Church, how many days does the Nativity Fast usually last in all?
explanation: Coptic tradition links the three days added to the original forty in the 10th century to the fast before the moving of the Mokattam mountain.
source: Coptic Orthodox calendar: Nativity Fast from 16 Hathor (25 November) to the eve of the Nativity (6 January)

question: The Coptic Kiahk praises prepare the faithful for which feast?
explanation: Kiahk is known as the Marian month, and its "Seven and Four" praises (seven Theotokias and four canticles) fill long, joyful vigils honoring the Virgin Mary.
source: Coptic Orthodox Psalmody (Tasbeha) for the month of Kiahk

question: On which mountain is the Transfiguration traditionally believed to have happened?
explanation: The Gospels say only "a high mountain," where Moses and Elijah appeared with Jesus; the Copts celebrate the feast on 13 Mesra (19 August).
source: Matthew 17:1–9; Coptic Orthodox calendar: Transfiguration on 13 Mesra (19 August)

question: The Saturday before Palm Sunday is named after which man Jesus raised from the dead?
explanation: Lazarus had been in the tomb four days, and news of this sign drew the crowds who welcomed Jesus into Jerusalem on Palm Sunday (John 11:17; 12:17–18).
source: John 11:1–44; 12:17–18; Coptic and Eastern Orthodox calendars (Lazarus Saturday)

question: On which day of Holy Week do Copts pray the Lakan, recalling Jesus washing feet?
explanation: The Lakan (basin) service blesses water and is prayed only three times a year: at Theophany, on Covenant Thursday and on the Feast of the Apostles.
source: John 13:1–17; Coptic Orthodox Holy Week (Pascha) rite: Lakan of Covenant Thursday

question: During the Coptic vigil called "Apocalypse Night," which book is read in full?
explanation: Through the night between Good Friday and the dawn of Bright Saturday, the whole book is read in a single service, a rare tradition in Christian worship.
source: Coptic Orthodox Holy Week (Pascha) rite: Bright Saturday (Apocalypse Night)

question: Which feast does the Coptic Church keep on 24 Bashans (1 June)?
options: Entry of the Lord into Egypt
explanation: Copts treasure Isaiah 19:1, "the Lord... will come into Egypt," and many churches and monasteries mark the Holy Family's traditional route.
source: Matthew 2:13–15; Isaiah 19:1; Coptic Orthodox calendar: Entry of the Lord into Egypt, 24 Bashans (1 June)

question: How many Major Feasts of the Lord does the Coptic Church celebrate?
explanation: They are the Annunciation, Nativity, Theophany, Palm Sunday, Resurrection, Ascension and Pentecost, with seven Minor Feasts of the Lord alongside them.
source: Coptic Orthodox calendar: seven Major and seven Minor Feasts of the Lord (copticchurch.net feast calendar)

question: What is the strict fast day just before the Nativity or Theophany called in Coptic tradition?
explanation: Depending on which weekday the feast falls, the Paramoun can stretch over more than one day of strict fasting.
source: Coptic Orthodox fasting tradition: Paramoun before the Nativity and Theophany

question: Which Gospel writer is traditionally represented by a lion?
explanation: The four Gospel symbols are the human for Matthew, lion for Mark, ox for Luke, and eagle for John.
source: Traditional Christian iconography of the four evangelists

question: In the account of Jesus’ baptism, the Holy Spirit descends like which bird?
explanation: The Gospel describes the Spirit of God descending like a dove and coming upon Jesus.
source: Matthew 3:16

question: The early Christian fish symbol is known by which Greek word?
explanation: Its letters spell out "Jesus Christ, Son of God, Savior" in Greek: Iēsous Christos Theou Yios Sōtēr.
source: Early Christian acrostic ΙΧΘΥΣ; Augustine, City of God 18.23

question: John the Baptist called Jesus "the ___ of God." Which animal completes his words?
explanation: The image recalls the Passover lamb, and in the Coptic liturgy the bread chosen for the offering is itself called the "Lamb."
source: John 1:29; Coptic Liturgy of St. Basil (the choosing of the Lamb)

question: In icons, what does the golden halo around a saint's head show?
explanation: In many Orthodox icons, Christ's own halo also holds a cross and the Greek letters Ο Ω Ν, "He who is" (Exodus 3:14).
source: Orthodox iconographic convention; Exodus 3:14 (Septuagint: ὁ ὤν)

question: Christ is called "the Alpha and the Omega." What does that title mean?
explanation: Alpha and Omega are the first and last letters of the Greek alphabet, so the title proclaims that Christ is before all things and completes all things.
source: Revelation 22:13; Revelation 1:8

question: What is the vessel on chains, swung to offer incense in church, called?
explanation: The rising smoke pictures prayer rising to God: "Let my prayer be set before You as incense" (Psalm 141:2).
source: Psalm 141:2; Revelation 8:3–4

question: In icons and church art, an apostle holding keys is usually which saint?
explanation: The keys recall Jesus' words to Peter: "I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven" (Matthew 16:19).
source: Matthew 16:19; traditional Christian iconography

question: The Chi-Rho symbol is made from what?
explanation: Chi (X) and Rho (P) begin the Greek word Christos, and Emperor Constantine famously placed the sign on his soldiers' shields and standard.
source: Lactantius, On the Deaths of the Persecutors 44; Eusebius, Life of Constantine 1.31

question: In the Roman catacombs, the anchor was a Christian symbol of what?
explanation: Hebrews calls hope "an anchor of the soul, both sure and steadfast," and the anchor's crossbar also made it a quiet, hidden cross.
source: Hebrews 6:19; early Christian catacomb art

question: In Christian art, a saint holding a palm branch is usually being honored as what?
explanation: Palms signal victory: Revelation describes a great multitude in white robes holding palm branches before God's throne (Revelation 7:9, 14).
source: Revelation 7:9–14; traditional Christian iconography

question: On icons of Christ, what do the letters IC XC stand for?
explanation: They abbreviate the Greek ΙΗΣΟΥΣ ΧΡΙΣΤΟΣ using the first and last letter of each name, with the Greek sigma written in its old "C" shape.
source: Byzantine and Orthodox icon inscription convention

question: Icons of Christ "Pantocrator" present Him as what?
explanation: One of the oldest surviving Pantocrator icons, painted in the 6th century, is kept at St. Catherine's Monastery in Sinai, Egypt.
source: Greek Pantokratōr, "Almighty" (Revelation 1:8); Sinai Pantocrator icon, St. Catherine's Monastery

question: Which bird, said in legend to feed its young with its own blood, became a symbol of Christ?
explanation: The Eucharistic hymn "Adoro te devote," traditionally credited to St. Thomas Aquinas, even addresses Christ as "loving Pelican."
source: Physiologus; hymn "Adoro te devote" ("Pie pellicane, Iesu Domine")

question: On many Orthodox icons of the Virgin Mary, the letters ΜΡ ΘΥ mean what?
explanation: The title Theotokos was championed by St. Cyril of Alexandria and affirmed at the Council of Ephesus in 431.
source: Greek Μήτηρ Θεοῦ; Council of Ephesus (431)

question: What is the icon-covered screen in front of the altar area called?
explanation: In Coptic churches the holy sanctuary behind it is called the haikal, and the screen often displays icons of Christ, the Virgin Mary and the apostles.
source: Orthodox church architecture; Coptic term haikal (sanctuary)

question: The evangelists' four creature symbols come from visions in Ezekiel and which other book?
explanation: St. Jerome's pairing (man, lion, ox, eagle for Matthew, Mark, Luke, John) became the usual one, though St. Irenaeus had earlier matched them differently.
source: Ezekiel 1:10; Revelation 4:6–8; Jerome, Commentary on Matthew (preface); Irenaeus, Against Heresies 3.11.8

question: Which pair of animals traditionally flanks St. Mina (Menas) in Coptic icons?
explanation: Tradition says the camels carrying his body stopped and would not move near Lake Mariout, marking his burial place, where the great pilgrimage site of Abu Mena later grew.
source: Coptic tradition of St. Mina (Menas); Abu Mena pilgrimage site near Alexandria

question: Which martyr is called "Abu Sefein" and shown in icons holding two swords?
explanation: Coptic tradition says an angel gave him a second, shining sword before battle: one his soldier's sword, the other a sword of divine power.
source: Coptic Synaxarium, 25 Hathor (St. Mercurius, Abu Sefein)

question: Early Egyptian Christians adapted which ancient symbol into a looped cross?
explanation: The ankh had long meant "life," and as the crux ansata it became a cross pointing to new life in Christ, especially common in Coptic textiles.
source: Coptic Christian art (crux ansata); Socrates Scholasticus, Church History 5.17
